title: SWAD: Domain Generalization by Seeking Flat Minima
mechanism: Dense stochastic weight averaging over a loss-plateau window of training gives flatter minima and better unseen-domain accuracy.
adaptation: Average weights every 100 steps from about 8k to 20k in house and PF runs; window chosen on F51 / val loss, never on test. Recompute BN stats on train after averaging. Targets E1 (new modules, half-cut, scuff).
evidence: +1.6 points average out-of-domain accuracy over prior SOTA on PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, DomainNet (classification).
min_experiment: In-run arm: same PF runs s5-9 save raw and SWAD weights (paired within run). Metric: val relF1@2 and F51 crack AP, then E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU at an opening. Kill if SWAD - raw < +0.005 val relF1@2 paired and E1 not better.
prior_overlap: none. Ensembling 5 seeds was tested (only clear win); weight averaging within a run was never run (BRIEF section 5 lists EMA / SWA as never varied).

alt_notes.adaptation: Average PF weights every 200 steps from 10k to 20k, recompute BN on train. Near-free; may also reduce the 1-in-6 wrecked-run variance.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + SWAD vs PF final checkpoint, same 3 seeds. Kill if test crack IoU gain < +0.01 and E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.
